text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPaleontologyThe Ancient Mammal That Changes Our Understanding of Dinosaur OriginsTanzania’s Nyasasaurus may not have been the first dinosaur on Earth after allDRBy Devin Reese2:00 PM CDT on September 16, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe earliest known dinosaurs lived in Tanzania 240 million years ago—at least that was the best evidence-based hypothesis until yesterday, which is when the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology published a new study that now shifts the scientific understanding of dinosaur origins.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 4D Dirac electrons observed at light speed, sparking potential for quantum computingShareNextStayThe study describes a set of fossils, originally excavated from the Manda fossil beds in what is now southwestern Tanzania during a 1963 British expedition, that were stored at the Natural History Museum in London. Initial research showed that they belonged to a group of mammal ancestors called dicynodonts that were common during the Triassic, before dinosaurs rose to prominence. Read more: “The Dainty Dinosaur That’s Rewriting Evolutionary History”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
